paper.title: A "quantum" Ramsey theorem for operator systems
paper.author: Nik Weaver
paper.affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Washington University, Saint Louis, MO 63130
paper.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 145 (2017), pp. 4595-4605
paper.abstract: Let \(\mathcal V\) be a linear subspace of \(M_n(\mathbb C)\) which contains the identity matrix and is stable under the formation of Hermitian adjoints. We prove that if \(n\) is sufficiently large then there exists a rank \(k\) orthogonal projection \(P\) such that \(\dim(P\mathcal V P) = 1\) or \(k^2\).
paper.context: Posed as Severini's question — a quantum analogue of the classical Ramsey theorem. An operator system in finite dimensions is a unital, *-closed linear subspace \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n(\mathbb C)\). In quantum error correction, operator systems play the role classically played by confusability graphs.

items.title: Quantum k-clique / quantum k-anticlique
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) be an operator system. A quantum k-clique of \(\mathcal V\) is an orthogonal projection \(P \in M_n\) (i.e., \(P = P^2 = P^*\)) whose rank is \(k\), such that \(P\mathcal V P = \{PAP : A \in \mathcal V\}\) is maximal; that is, \(P\mathcal V P = PM_nP \cong M_k\), or equivalently, \(\dim(P\mathcal V P) = k^2\). A quantum k-anticlique of \(\mathcal V\) is a rank \(k\) projection \(P\) such that \(P\mathcal V P\) is minimal; that is, \(P\mathcal V P = \mathbb C\cdot P \cong M_1\), or equivalently, \(\dim(P\mathcal V P) = 1\).
items.note: The anticlique definition matches the quantum-error-correction notion of a code: the range of a projection \(P\) with \(P\mathcal V P = \mathbb C\cdot P\) [3].

items.title: Diagonal system has no quantum anticlique (k ≥ 2)
items.proof_sketch: If \(P\) has rank \(k \geq 2\), then since each \(\mathrm{rank}(E_{ii})=1\), each \(\mathrm{rank}(PE_{ii}P) \in \{0,1\}\). They cannot all be zero (else \(P = \sum PE_{ii}P = 0\)). Pick \(i\) with rank-1 \(PE_{ii}P\); it cannot lie in \(\mathbb C\cdot P\) (which has rank 0 or \(k\)), so \(PD_nP \neq \mathbb C\cdot P\).

items.title: Diagonal system has a quantum k-clique when n is large
items.statement: If \(n \geq k^2 + k - 1\) then \(D_n\) has a quantum \(k\)-clique.
items.proof_sketch: Take \(n = k^2 + k - 1\). Pick \(k^2\) vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_{k^2} \in \mathbb C^k\) whose rank-1 outer products \(v_iv_i^*\) span \(M_k\) (e.g. \(e_i\), \(e_i+e_j\), \(e_i+ie_j\)). Identify \(\mathbb C^n \cong \mathbb C^k \oplus \mathbb C^{k^2-1}\) and extend each \(v_i\) to a mutually orthogonal \(w_i \in \mathbb C^n\) by appending a triangular block. Let \(P\) project onto \(\mathbb C^k\); then \(P D_n P\) (relative to the basis \(w_i/\|w_i\|\)) contains \(v_iv_i^*\), so \(\dim(PD_nP) = k^2\).
items.note: Improved later in Lemma 4.3. Note \(n \geq k^2\) is necessary since \(\dim(D_n)=n\) but \(\dim(PD_nP) = k^2\) is required.

items.title: Arbitrarily large systems may lack quantum 3-cliques
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V_n = \mathrm{span}\{I_n, E_{11}, E_{12}, \ldots, E_{1n}, E_{21}, \ldots, E_{n1}\} \subseteq M_n\). Then \(\mathcal V_n\) has no quantum 3-cliques.
items.proof_sketch: For any projection \(P\): if \(Pe_1 = 0\) then \(PE_{1i}P = PE_{i1}P = 0\) and \(P\) is an anticlique. Otherwise, in an orthonormal basis \(f_1=Pe_1/\|Pe_1\|, f_2,\ldots,f_k\) of \(\mathrm{ran}(P)\), the compression \(P\mathcal V_nP\) is exactly \(\mathcal V_k \subseteq M_k\), of dimension \(2k\). For \(k \geq 3\), \(2k < k^2\), so \(P\) is not a clique.

items.title: Low-dimensional orthocomplement is spanned by rank-2 Hermitians
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) be an operator system and suppose \(\dim(\mathcal V) \leq 3\). Then its Hilbert-Schmidt orthocomplement is spanned by rank-2 Hermitian matrices.
items.proof_sketch: Work in \(M_n^h\). Suppose \(B \in \mathcal V_0^\perp\) is Hermitian, nonzero, and orthogonal to the real span \(\mathcal W_0\) of rank-2 Hermitians in \(\mathcal V_0^\perp\). Decompose \(B = B_+ - B_-\) (positive/negative parts), \(\alpha = \mathrm{Tr}(B_+) = \mathrm{Tr}(B_-)\). By convexity of the joint numerical range of three Hermitian matrices [1], pick unit vectors \(v, w\) with \(\langle Av,v\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\mathrm{Tr}(AB_+)\) and \(\langle Aw,w\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\mathrm{Tr}(AB_-)\) for \(A \in \{A_1, A_2, B\}\). Then \(C = \alpha(vv^* - ww^*)\) is rank-2 Hermitian, lies in \(\mathcal W_0\), and is not orthogonal to \(B\) — contradiction.

items.title: Four-dimensional V ⊆ M₃ has a quantum 2-clique
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_3\) be an operator system and suppose \(\dim(\mathcal V) = 4\). Then \(\mathcal V\) has a quantum 2-clique.
items.proof_sketch: Write \(\mathcal V = \mathrm{span}\{I_3, A_1, A_2, A_3\}\) with \(A_i\) Hermitian. Diagonalize \(A_1\) so it has the form \(\mathrm{diag}(0, 1, a)\), and normalize \(A_2, A_3\) so their \((i,i)\)-entries vanish for \(i \leq 2\). With \(v = (1,\alpha,0)^T\), \(w = (1,0,\beta)^T\), the \(4\times 4\) matrix of inner products \(\langle A_iv,v\rangle, \langle A_iv,w\rangle, \langle A_iw,v\rangle, \langle A_iw,w\rangle\) has a nonzero determinant (polynomial in \(\alpha, \beta\)) unless one of \(A_2, A_3\) is a scalar multiple of the other.

items.title: Quantum 2-cliques exist when dim(V) ≥ 4
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) be an operator system and suppose \(\dim(\mathcal V) \geq 4\). Then \(\mathcal V\) has a quantum 2-clique.
items.proof_sketch: WLOG \(\dim(\mathcal V) = 4\), \(\mathcal V = \mathrm{span}\{I_n, A_1, A_2, A_3\}\). Find a rank-\(\leq 3\) projection \(P\) so that \(PI_nP, PA_1P, PA_2P\) are linearly independent (split on whether \(A_1, A_2\) are jointly diagonalizable). Pick \(B \in M_n\) making the compression 4-dimensional and apply Lemma 3.2 to get a rank-2 \(Q \leq P\) with \(\{QI_nQ, QA_1Q, QA_2Q, QBQ\}\) independent. If \(\{QI_nQ, QA_1Q, QA_2Q, QA_3Q\}\) is also independent, done; otherwise use Lemma 3.1 to find a rank-2 Hermitian \(C = vv^* - ww^*\) detecting \(A_3\); extend \(Q\) by \(v\) (or \(w\)) to a rank-3 \(Q'\) on which the four compressions are independent, then re-apply Lemma 3.2.
items.note: Sharp: the result fails for arbitrary 4-dim subspaces, e.g. \(\mathrm{span}\{E_{11},E_{12},E_{13},E_{14}\} \subset M_4\) has no rank-2 \(P\) with \(\dim(P\mathcal V P) > 2\).

items.title: Diagonal-contained systems: dimension thresholds for cliques/anticliques
items.statement: Suppose the operator system \(\mathcal V\) is contained in \(D_n\). If \(\dim(\mathcal V) \geq k^2 + k - 1\) then \(\mathcal V\) has a quantum \(k\)-clique. If \(\dim(\mathcal V) \leq \frac{n-k}{k-1}\) then \(\mathcal V\) has a quantum \(k\)-anticlique. If \(n \geq k^3 - k + 1\) then \(\mathcal V\) has either a quantum \(k\)-clique or a quantum \(k\)-anticlique.
items.proof_sketch: Clique case: choose \(m = k^2+k-1\) indices on which \(\mathcal V\) compresses faithfully, then invoke Prop 2.2. Anticlique case: Tverberg's generalization of Radon's theorem [6, 7], packaged as in Theorem 4 of [4]. Combining the two cases gives the cubic-in-\(k\) threshold via a little algebra.

items.title: Gramian-extension to make vectors orthonormal-of-equal-norm
items.statement: Let \(v_1, \ldots, v_r \in \mathbb C^s\). Then there are vectors \(w_1, \ldots, w_r \in \mathbb C^{r-1}\) such that the vectors \(v_i \oplus w_i \in \mathbb C^{s+r-1}\) are pairwise orthogonal and all have the same norm.
items.proof_sketch: Let \(G\) be the Gramian of \((v_i)\). Since \(\mathrm{rank}(\|G\|I_r - G) \leq r-1\), one can realize \(\|G\|I_r - G\) as the Gramian of some \(w_i \in \mathbb C^{r-1}\). The Gramian of \((v_i \oplus w_i)\) is then \(\|G\|I_r\).

items.title: Quantum k-clique from upper-triangular-supported Hermitians (improves Prop 2.2)
items.statement: Let \(n = k^2 + k - 1\) and suppose \(A_1, \ldots, A_{k^2}\) are Hermitian matrices in \(M_n\) such that for each \(i\), \(\langle A_ie_i, e_i\rangle = 1\), and \(\langle A_ie_r, e_s\rangle = 0\) whenever \(\max\{r,s\} > i\). Then \(\mathcal V = \mathrm{span}\{I, A_1, \ldots, A_{k^2}\}\) has a quantum \(k\)-clique.
items.proof_sketch: Inductively pick \(v_1, \ldots, v_{k^2} \in \mathbb C^k\) so the compressions \(A_i' = \sum_{r,s \leq i} a_{rs}^i v_r v_s^*\) are linearly independent. The freedom \(\tilde u = u + v_i\) in writing \(A_i' = B' + \tilde u\tilde u^*\) suffices because rank-1 updates span \(M_k\). Then use Lemma 4.2 to assemble an orthonormal-of-equal-norm extension \(f_i = (v_i \oplus w_i)/N\), yielding the desired clique.

items.title: Quantum k-clique from off-diagonal-supported matrices (technical)
items.statement: Let \(n = k^4 + k^3 + k - 1\) and \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) an operator system containing matrices \(A_1, \ldots, A_{k^4+k^3}\) with \(\langle A_ie_i, e_{i+1}\rangle \neq 0\) and \(\langle A_ie_r, e_s\rangle = 0\) when \(\max\{r,s\} > i+1\) and \(r \neq s\). Then \(\mathcal V\) has a quantum \(k\)-clique.
items.proof_sketch: Either some block of \(k^2+k-1\) matrices has linearly independent \(r\)-tails — then Lemma 4.1 gives a diagonal-style \(k\)-clique — or one can construct orthonormal \(v_1, \ldots, v_{k^2}\) and Hermitian \(B_1, \ldots, B_{k^2} \in \mathcal V\) whose compressions to \(\mathrm{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_{k^2}, e_{k^4+k^3+1}, \ldots, e_{k^4+k^3+k-1}\}\) satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma 4.3.

items.title: MAIN THEOREM — quantum Ramsey for operator systems
items.statement: Every operator system in \(M_{8k^{11}}\) has either a quantum \(k\)-clique or a quantum \(k\)-anticlique.
items.proof_sketch: Set \(n = 8k^{11}\). Iteratively pick unit vectors \(v_1, v_2, \ldots\) so that \(\dim((\mathcal V v_1)^\perp \cap \cdots \cap (\mathcal V v_{r-1})^\perp \cap (\mathcal V v_r)) < 8k^8\). If the construction lasts \(k^3\) steps, the compression to \(\mathrm{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_{k^3}\} \cong M_{k^3}\) sits inside \(D_{k^3}\), so Lemma 4.1 supplies a clique or anticlique. Otherwise, in the residual subspace \(F\), build a chain \(w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_r\) and matrices \(A_1, \ldots, A_{r-1} \in \mathcal V'\) with \(w_{r+1} = A_r w_r\) orthogonal to \(\mathrm{span}\{w_j, A_iw_j, A_i^* w_j : i<r, j\leq r\}\) (dimension \(\leq 2r^2 - r\)). For \(r \leq 2k^4\), this fits in \(8k^8\). Compress to \(\mathrm{span}(w_i)\) and apply Lemma 4.4 with \(n = 2k^4\).
items.note: The constants can be improved only marginally. Determining optimal bounds on quantum Ramsey numbers is likely open-ended, as in the classical case.

items.title: Quantum graph on M (from [8, Def 2.6(d)])
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a unital *-subalgebra of \(M_n\). A quantum graph on \(\mathcal M\) is an operator system \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) which satisfies \(\mathcal M' \mathcal V \mathcal M' = \mathcal V\).
items.note: Representation-independent: ∗-isomorphic \(\mathcal M, \mathcal N\) give a natural correspondence of quantum graphs ([8, Thm 2.7]).

items.title: Quantum k-clique / k-anticlique relative to M
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal M \subseteq M_n\) be a unital *-subalgebra and \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) a quantum graph on \(\mathcal M\). A rank \(k\) projection \(P \in \mathcal M\) is a quantum k-clique if \(P\mathcal V P = PM_nP\), and a quantum k-anticlique if \(P\mathcal V P = P\mathcal M'P\).
items.note: Crucially, \(P\) must belong to \(\mathcal M\). When \(\mathcal M = M_n\), this reduces to Definition 1.1; when \(\mathcal M = D_n\), it reproduces the classical k-clique/k-anticlique notions.

items.title: Quantum Ramsey for quantum graphs of the form M_n ⊗ I_d
items.statement: Let \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_{nd} \cong M_n \otimes M_d\) be a quantum graph on \(M_n \otimes I_d\). If \(nd \geq 8k^{11}\) then there is a projection in \(M_n \otimes I_d\) whose rank is at least \(k\) and which is either a quantum clique or a quantum anticlique of \(\mathcal V\).
items.proof_sketch: \(\mathcal V = \mathcal W \otimes M_d\) for some operator system \(\mathcal W \subseteq M_n\). If \(d=1\), apply Thm 4.5. If \(d \geq k\), any \(P \otimes I_d\) with rank-1 \(P\) works. For \(2 \leq d < k\): algebra shows \(n \geq 8\lceil k/d \rceil^{11}\), so Thm 4.5 gives a quantum \(\lceil k/d\rceil\)-clique/anticlique \(Q \in M_n\), and \(Q \otimes I_d\) is the required object.
items.note: Can only promise rank \(\geq k\), since ranks in \(M_n \otimes I_d\) are multiples of \(d\).

items.title: Common generalization of classical and quantum Ramsey theorems
items.statement: For every \(k\) there exists \(n\) such that if \(\mathcal M\) is a unital *-subalgebra of \(M_n\) and \(\mathcal V \subseteq M_n\) is an operator system satisfying \(\mathcal M' \mathcal V \mathcal M' = \mathcal V\), then there is a projection \(P \in \mathcal M\) whose rank is at least \(k\) and such that \(P\mathcal V P = PM_nP\) or \(P\mathcal M'P\).
items.proof_sketch: Take \(n = 8k^{11} \cdot R(k,k)\) where \(R(k,k)\) is the classical Ramsey number. Write \(\mathcal M = \bigoplus_{i=1}^r (M_{n_i} \otimes I_{d_i})\). If \(r \leq R(k,k)\), some \(n_i d_i \geq 8k^{11}\) and Lemma 5.3 applies to that block. If \(r > R(k,k)\), pick rank-1 \(Q_i \in M_{n_i}\), let \(Q = \bigoplus Q_i \otimes I_{d_i}\); then \(Q\mathcal V Q\) corresponds to a simple graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,r\}\) by [8, Thm 2.7]; the classical Ramsey theorem applied to \(G\) yields the required diagonal projection.
items.note: Recovers Thm 4.5 when \(\mathcal M = M_n\), and the classical Ramsey theorem when \(\mathcal M = D_n\) (both with worse constants). The gap between classical (exponential growth) and quantum (polynomial growth) Ramsey numbers is explained in the discussion: the classical bound's exponential dependence comes from needing \(\mathcal Wv\) of small codimension rather than large dimension.
